turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: Hi, thanks for coming in today. What's been going on for you lately?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It's... just been a lot, I guess. Work's been keeping me up at night, and then I'll be thinking about my health, or my mom's health, and whether I should've said that one thing to my boss, and... (pauses) I don't know, it's just stuff.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: That sounds like a lot to deal with. Can you tell me more about what you're thinking about with your boss and your mom's health?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighs) Oh, it's just... my boss was acting weird the other day, and I worry that I might've done something wrong. And my mom's been complaining about this pain in her side, and I keep thinking about all the things that could be wrong with her. (pauses, looks away) It's stupid, I know. I'm sure it's just nothing. But my mind just won't stop. (looks back, fidgets)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's understandable that you're worried about your boss and your mom's health. It's natural to have concerns and thoughts about them. Can you tell me more about why you think it's stupid and why you're sure it's nothing?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (fidgets, looks down) I don't know... it's just that my mind always goes to the worst-case scenario. And then I'm thinking, "Is it normal to be worried about this?" And I'll ask someone, like my partner, and they'll say, "Yeah, it's normal to worry," but then I'll start thinking, "But what if I'm not normal?" (looks up, slightly defensive) It's just really hard to shake these thoughts.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I see. It sounds like you have a tendency to overthink and worry about potential negative outcomes. This can be a common experience for many people, and it doesn't necessarily mean that there's something wrong with you. Can you tell me more about what it feels like to have these thoughts and how they impact your daily life?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighs, looks away) It's like... my mind is always racing, and I feel like I'm stuck in this constant state of tension. My shoulders are up by my ears half the day, and I'm always on edge, waiting for something bad to happen. It's like my brain is trying to warn me about all these potential disasters, but it's exhausting. I just want to be able to relax and not think about all this stuff, you know? (looks back, seems slightly irritated) But it's hard to turn it off.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: I understand. It sounds like you're experiencing a lot of anxiety and tension related to your thoughts and worries. This can be overwhelming and impactful on daily life. Have you sought help or support for these feelings before?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shrugs) I've talked to my partner about it, and they've been trying to be supportive. But it's hard for them to understand, I think. They'll tell me things like, "You're fine," or "Just relax," but it's not that easy. (pauses, looks down) I've also tried to talk to friends about it, but they just tell me to calm down or that I'm overreacting. It feels like nobody really gets it. (looks up, slightly annoyed) And even when I do try to talk about it, I feel like I'm just a bother or something.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It sounds like you've been seeking support from your partner and friends, but haven't felt fully understood or validated. This can be a challenging experience, as it's important to feel heard and understood when discussing mental health concerns. Have you considered seeking professional help, such as a therapist or counselor, to further address these feelings and concerns?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (sighs, looks away) Yeah, I've thought about it. But, I don't know... it's just so hard to even talk about this stuff, and I feel like it's going to sound silly or something. And, I don't know, it's just a lot of money, too. (pauses, looks back) But, at the same time, I feel like I'm just getting worse and worse. I'm exhausted all the time, and I just feel like I'm barely holding it together. (looks down, seems almost ashamed) Maybe I should try to get help, but it's just hard to take that first step.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's understandable that you're hesitant to seek professional help, but it's important to prioritize your well-being and address these feelings and concerns. Reaching out for help can be a significant step in managing anxiety and finding support. It's important to remember that seeking help doesn't mean there's something wrong with you, but rather that you're taking proactive steps to improve your mental health. Is there anything else you'd like to talk about or any questions you have about seeking help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looks up, slightly hesitant) I don't know... I just feel like I'm a burden, I guess. Like, I'm always worrying about everyone else, and now I'm supposed to worry about myself, too? (pauses, looks away) And what if I go to therapy and it doesn't work? What if I'm just stuck like this forever? (looks back, seems almost desperate) Is it... is it ever possible to just feel normal again?

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's understandable that you may feel like a burden or have concerns about seeking help, but it's important to remember that you deserve support and care for your mental health. Seeking help doesn't mean that you're a burden, but rather that you're taking steps to improve your well-being. It's also important to remember that therapy is a process and may take time to see results. However, it's possible to feel normal again and find relief from anxiety and worries with the right support. Is there anything else you'd like to discuss or any questions you have about seeking help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (shakes head slightly) No, I don't think so. I just... (pauses, looks down) I guess I just feel like I'm running out of steam, you know? Like, I'm constantly worried about something, and it's just exhausting. (looks back, seems almost pleading) Can't I just have a day where I don't have to think about anything? Just one day? (looks away, voice cracks slightly) Sorry.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's okay, human. It's understandable to feel overwhelmed and exhausted by these thoughts and worries. Seeking help and support can be a significant step in managing anxiety and finding relief. Remember, it's okay to ask for help and prioritize your own well-being. Is there anything else you'd like to talk about or any questions you have about seeking help?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (looks up, eyes welling up with tears) No... I think that's it. Just... thank you, I guess. For listening. (pauses, voice barely above a whisper) Sorry again.

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: It's okay, human. Thank you for sharing and for being open to discussing your feelings. Remember that seeking help is a positive step towards improving your mental health. Take care.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: (nods slightly, looking down) Thank you. I'll try. (pauses, then gets up and walks out of the room, still looking down)

turns.speaker: therapist
turns.text: (pauses, then looks down and nods slightly)
